text: dsh-mcp-relay 是把正在运行的 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）实例接入 MCP 客户端的插件。它在 DSH 内注册本机 HTTP 中继接口，并提供独立的 MCP stdio 服务，让外部 agent 能列出会话与模型、委派任务、等待结果、回答会话问题以及管理审批和取消当前轮次。适合希望从 Codex 等 MCP 客户端驱动 DSH 会话的用户；需要在同一台机器运行 DSH Web 与 Node.js 18 以上版本，并配置 MCP 客户端。

dsh-mcp-relay connects a running DeepSeek Harness (DSH) instance to MCP clients. Its local HTTP relay and MCP stdio server let agents list sessions, delegate tasks, collect results, answer questions, and cancel turns. Use it to drive DSH from Codex; DSH Web and Node.js 18+ run on the same machine.
想从 Codex 这样的 MCP 客户端调用我本机 DSH 的会话。
能不能让外部 agent 查看 DSH 会话并继续已有任务？
I want an MCP client to delegate work to sessions in my running DSH instance.
dsh-mcp-relay 的功能「委派并跟进 DSH 会话」：MCP 客户端可创建会话或用 sessionId 续接会话，提交工作区和指令；服务可等待任务完成、读取状态和输出，也能列出会话与当前实例可用模型。
dsh-mcp-relay 的功能「处理会话提问与审批」：在接管提问时，客户端可提交答案让 DSH agent 继续；还可设置后续审批的处理方式，并取消正在运行的轮次。

dsh-mcp-relay README · dsh-mcp-relay：[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

Expose a running [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) instance over the
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), so an external agent — Codex, or any MCP client —
can drive that instance's own sessions.

dsh-mcp-relay README · dsh-mcp-relay：A DSH session behaves like a subagent from the caller's point of view: it keeps its own context across calls,
works in the workspace you name, and returns a final answer. The relay also lets the caller answer the
questions that DSH agent asks, so a delegated task never deadlocks waiting for a human who is not there.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Why：Driving a DSH instance through its web GUI from another agent costs a screenshot or DOM round trip per step.
This relay replaces that with a small structured API: one tool call in, one result out.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Architecture：```
MCP client (stdio)
 └── bin/dsh-mcp-relay.mjs          MCP server; polls the relay, holds questions for the caller
      └── HTTP 127.0.0.1:<port>/dsh-relay
           └── lib/index.js    host Cordis plugin mounted inside the running DSH process

Two halves, and the split matters:

dsh-mcp-relay README · Architecture：- **`lib/index.js`** is a DSH host plugin. It runs in the same process as the Web GUI, so it can read and
  write the sessions that instance already has. It registers an HTTP route and does the DSH work.
- **`bin/dsh-mcp-relay.mjs`** is a standalone MCP server that speaks stdio to your agent and HTTP to the plugin.
  It exists because DSH's own process owns stdout, so the plugin cannot serve stdio itself.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Architecture：Waiting and polling happen in the MCP server, where they cost nothing, and `dsh_delegate` blocks by default:
your model spends **one** tool call per delegated turn and receives the finished result.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Architecture：The tool surface is deliberately small. The handshake instructions and every tool schema are re-sent with
each model request, so each of them is a recurring cost rather than a one-off. Keep the default `wait: true`
and let it block — an async delegation that then gets short-polled costs one full request per poll.

dsh-mcp-relay README · What a Codex caller pays：An MCP client re-sends the handshake instructions and every tool schema with each model request, so that
text is a recurring cost rather than a one-off. Since 0.6.1 the surface is sized for that:

dsh-mcp-relay README · What a Codex caller pays：Waiting has a purpose rule, not just an interval rule: these tools exist to deliver a result, not progress
updates. Let `dsh_delegate` block unless you have independent work that can start now; finish that work,
then collect the result with `dsh_poll` and a long `timeoutMs`. A `timeout` ends the wait — it is not a
failure, and "still running" is not a reason to keep querying and narrating progress.

dsh-mcp-relay README · What a Codex caller pays：One limit sits outside this plugin: an MCP client may cap a single tool call (Codex exposes
`tool_timeout_sec`). A cap shorter than the relay's own wait turns one blocking delegation into repeated
round trips, and no prompt can undo that — give it at least `DSH_RELAY_TIMEOUT_MS`. For Codex:

```toml
[mcp_servers.dsh]
tool_timeout_sec = 600
```

The effect is measurable rather than asserted:

dsh-mcp-relay README · What a Codex caller pays：```bash
node bin/dsh-bench.mjs surface        # both sizes, plus the per-tool breakdown
node bin/dsh-bench.mjs usage <dir>    # attribute a Codex session's requests to dsh tool calls
```

`DSH_RELAY_SURFACE=full` serves the older, larger surface, so the same task can be run against both and
compared. The saving per request is small next to a long conversation's history; what matters is that it is
paid on *every* request rather than once.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Requirements：- DSH with a Web profile (`dsh web` or the desktop app).
- Node.js 18 or newer on the same machine as DSH.
- An MCP client that can spawn a stdio server.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Install the plugin：Install straight from this repository — the package is not published to npm:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Nigheart/dsh-mcp-relay
```

Then restart DSH. On startup the log should show:

```
[dsh-mcp-relay] mounted /dsh-relay (tokenRequired=false)
```

Verify it independently:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-relay/ping

dsh-mcp-relay README · {"ok":true,"data":{"relay":"dsh-mcp-relay","version":"0.6.4","tokenRequired":false}}：```

If your instance listens on a port other than 3080, use that port here and set `DSH_RELAY_URL` for the MCP
server (below).

dsh-mcp-relay README · Manual install：The package ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts one loader row. That row declares
`inject: [webServer, sessionController]` — keep it. Without `inject` the plugin can be activated before those
services exist, find nothing to bind to, and mount no route at all.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Configure your MCP client：Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

```toml
[mcp_servers.dsh]
command = "node"
args = ["/absolute/path/to/dsh-mcp-relay/bin/dsh-mcp-relay.mjs"]
startup_timeout_sec = 60

dsh-mcp-relay README · Only needed when DSH is not on the default port, or when a token is set.：[mcp_servers.dsh.env]
DSH_RELAY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/dsh-relay"
```

The server sends its own usage notes in the MCP handshake (`initialize.instructions`), so the client learns
the workflow without any extra prompting.

Environment variables:
section: Only needed when DSH is not on the default port, or when a token is set.

text:
dsh-mcp-relay README · Only needed when DSH is not on the default port, or when a token is set.：| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_RELAY_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:3080/dsh-relay` | Where the plugin listens. |
| `DSH_RELAY_TOKEN` | *(unset)* | Sent as `x-dsh-relay-token`; must match the plugin's value. |
| `DSH_RELAY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `600000` | Default wait for one delegated turn. |
| `DSH_RELAY_POLL_MS` | `2000` | Progress poll interval. |
| `DSH_RELAY_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` | `30000` | Per-request cap for relay calls; a hung relay fails the call instead of hanging the turn. |
| `DSH_RELAY_SURFACE` | `lean` | Tool surface to serve. `full` serves the frozen 0.6.0 surface, for A/B measurement only. |

text:
dsh-mcp-relay README · Tools：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `dsh_list_sessions` | List sessions of the running instance, optionally filtered to one workspace. |
| `dsh_models` | List the provider/model ids this instance can route, with each model's reasoning efforts. |
| `dsh_delegate` | Create a session in a workspace, or continue one by `sessionId`, send an instruction, and wait for that turn to finish. |
| `dsh_answer` | Answer a question the DSH agent asked, so it can resume. |
| `dsh_approval` | Choose how a session resolves **future** approval requests: `gui`, `auto-approve`, or `deny`. |
| `dsh_cancel` | Cancel the active turn — the way out of an approval nobody can answer. |
| `dsh_poll` | Read a session's status and latest output; use after a wait that returned `waiting` or `timeout`. |

dsh-mcp-relay README · Delegating work：```
dsh_delegate({ workspace: "/home/me/project", instruction: "Add the missing tests for parser.js" })
```

By default the call **blocks** until the turn ends — that is the intended path: one request in, one result
out. Pass `wait: false` only when you have other work to do in parallel; then collect the result with
`dsh_poll` and a long `timeoutMs`, never a one-second loop.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Delegating work：Omit `sessionId` to start a new DSH agent; pass the returned `sessionId` back to continue the **same** agent,
which still remembers the earlier work. `status` tells you what happened:

| `status` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `completed` | The turn finished; `output` holds the agent's final answer. |
| `waiting` | Blocked on a human: either a question takeover is holding for you, or an open approval request. |
| `timeout` | Still running; call `dsh_poll` with the same `baselineSeq`. |

dsh-mcp-relay README · Delegating work：The relay also attaches every session it creates (or reuses) to the DSH workspace owning the target
directory. DSH groups sessions in its GUI by that explicit attachment rather than by working directory, so
without it a delegated session runs fine but shows up as *ungrouped*. Sessions created before this behaviour
existed can be repaired with one call to the relay's `POST /dsh-relay/attach-all` endpoint.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Choosing the model：A session runs on the instance's default model unless you say otherwise. `dsh_models` reports what this
instance can route right now — provider groups, model ids, and each model's reasoning efforts:

```
dsh_models()
dsh_delegate({ workspace: "/home/me/project", instruction: "…",
               model: "deepseek-v4.1-pro", reasoningEffort: "high" })
```

dsh-mcp-relay README · Choosing the model：`model` takes a model id; `provider` is inferred when that id is unambiguous, and `provider/model` is
always accepted. `reasoningEffort` must be one of the efforts `dsh_models` lists for that model. A route
this instance cannot serve fails the call *before* the instruction is sent, rather than quietly running
it on some other model.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Choosing the model：The selection applies to this turn and is also saved as the instance default for sessions created
without one — the same stickiness DSH's own model picker has, so choose deliberately. Omit `model` to
leave the session on whatever it already uses. `dsh_delegate` echoes the selection it installed as
`model` (with `modelNote`); `dsh_list_sessions` and `dsh_poll` report each session's current `model`,
read from DSH's model-selection projection (a hint: it is `null` until the session has recorded a
request, and on deployments without that projection).

dsh-mcp-relay README · Answering questions：By default a delegated session runs under **takeover**: when the DSH agent calls its question tool, the call is
suspended and handed to the caller instead of the GUI. `dsh_delegate` then returns immediately with the
question rather than waiting:

```json
{
  "status": "waiting",
  "waiting": {
    "kind": "user-question",

Answer it with the ids from `detail`:

```
dsh_answer({ sessionId, answers: [{ id: "choice", selected: ["sqlite"] }] })
```

dsh-mcp-relay README · Answering questions：If nobody answers within about three minutes, the question falls back to the DSH GUI, so an unattended
delegation cannot hang forever. Pass `takeover: false` to `dsh_delegate` to leave questions with the GUI from
the start.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Approvals：Some operations need a decision before DSH will run them — for example escalating a sandbox so a tool can write
outside the session workspace. The session then reports:

```json
{
  "status": "waiting",
  "waiting": {
    "kind": "approval",

`reason` is DSH's own explanation of what it wants and why, so the caller can judge whether granting it is
appropriate.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Approvals：**An approval that is already pending has only two exits**: a person answers it in the DSH Web GUI, or the turn
is abandoned with `dsh_cancel`. Nothing below can rescue the request that is already open.

`dsh_approval({ sessionId, mode })` decides how **future** approvals in that session are handled. The policy
takes effect at the agent's next step, so it never applies retroactively:

dsh-mcp-relay README · Approvals：- `"gui"` (the default) — leave them to the DSH Web GUI for a person to answer.
- `"deny"` — set the session's policy to `never`: every subsequent request resolves as rejected without
  prompting. For unattended work this beats waiting forever — a clean failure instead of a hang.
- `"auto-approve"` — this plugin answers the request itself with a one-shot grant. Whether that is even possible
  is deployment-dependent: the plugin has to sit **upstream** of the GUI's answerer. Registering the mode is
  therefore **not** proof that it works — check the relay's `/dsh-relay/diagnostics`
  (`approvalListener.listenerHits`); the endpoint reports `effective: false` with a warning when it cannot. On
  the deployment this was built against, `listenerHits` is 0, so only `deny` and `gui` take effect there.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Approvals：A tool call that has simply not finished yet is **not** reported as `waiting`; such a session stays `running`
and carries an informational `pendingTool` field.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Security：The relay is a control surface: whoever can reach it can send instructions to, and read the history of, every
session in that DSH instance.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Security：- It **serves loopback callers only** and answers `403` to anything else. This matters because the shipped Web
  profile binds `0.0.0.0`.
- Set `DSH_RELAY_TOKEN` on both sides to additionally require an `x-dsh-relay-token` header.
- The route is registered directly on DSH's HTTP server, so it is **not** covered by the `/api` trusted-host
  fence. Its own checks above are the only gate.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Limitations：- The MCP server and DSH must run on the same machine, because the relay is loopback-only.
- One delegated turn is bounded by `DSH_RELAY_TIMEOUT_MS`; there is no streaming of partial output.
- `cancel` stops the active turn only — messages already queued in DSH keep running.
- The plugin reads a session's tail through `sessionController.page`, so a very large session reports its
  recent history rather than all of it.

dsh-mcp-relay README · Development：The plugin can be developed without restarting DSH: load it as a dynamic Cordis plugin first, verify behaviour
against the live services, then install it as a bundle package. Do finish with one real restart — dynamic
plugins are activated only after the services they need already exist, so they cannot catch a startup-order
bug such as a missing `inject`.

The relay's route table has a dependency-free test that stubs the Cordis context, so it needs neither DSH nor
a restart:

```bash
npm test
```

dsh-mcp-relay README · Development：The tool surface is measurable. `node bin/dsh-bench.mjs surface` prints both variants' instruction and
schema sizes; `node bin/dsh-bench.mjs usage <session.jsonl>` attributes a Codex session's model requests to
the dsh tool calls inside it. Serve the frozen surface with `DSH_RELAY_SURFACE=full` to run the same task
against both.
